t: You're standing at the Grand Staircase of the Foreign Office, looking at the Empire Murals, a series of frescoes painted by the English artist Sigismund Goetze. He worked on them between 1912 and 1921, and he meant them as a work of public service. They were criticised at the time, though. In 2020, questions were raised again about whether an artwork showing dated attitudes to race and empire belongs in a building of such political importance. Goetze himself was born in London.
